items.followUp: Define oscillatory motion and give one example.

rubric.why: The definition must show motion back and forth about a central position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing to-and-fro motion about a mean position.

rubric.why: A correct example completes the definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any suitable example.

modelAnswer: Vibratory motion is the to-and-fro motion of a body about its mean position.
The vibrations of a tuning fork are an example.

items.followUp: State Newton's first law of motion and give two examples of it.

rubric.why: The law requires equal and opposite forces acting on different bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that action and reaction are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.

rubric.why: The question asks for two examples illustrating the law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two suitable examples.

modelAnswer: When one body exerts a force on another body, the second body exerts an equal and opposite force on the first body.
Examples include the recoil of a gun and walking.

items.followUp: What is meant by the normal reaction of a surface?

rubric.why: Tension is a pulling force present in a stretched string.
rubric.description: Identifies tension as a force in a stretched string.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing tension as the pulling force in a stretched string.

rubric.why: The tension acts along the length of the string.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it acts along the string.

modelAnswer: Tension is the pulling force exerted by a stretched string on an attached body.
It acts along the length of the string.

items.followUp: Define limiting friction and write its relation with the coefficient of friction and normal reaction.

rubric.why: The coefficient is defined as the ratio of limiting friction to normal reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the ratio of limiting friction to normal reaction.

rubric.why: The equation expresses the required ratio.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation, with F as limiting friction and R as normal reaction.

modelAnswer: The coefficient of friction is the ratio of limiting friction to the normal reaction.
μ = F/R, where F is the limiting friction and R is the normal reaction.

items.followUp: Why is the centre of gravity kept low in racing cars?

rubric.why: The distribution of mass makes the centre of gravity lower.
rubric.description: Identifies the lower centre of gravity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that vehicles are made heavier at the bottom to lower their centre of gravity.

rubric.why: A lower centre of gravity improves stability and reduces the risk of overturning.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking this design to greater stability or reduced overturning.

modelAnswer: Vehicles are made heavy at the bottom to keep their centre of gravity low.
A low centre of gravity increases stability and reduces the chance of overturning.

items.followUp: What is meant by stable equilibrium?

rubric.why: Equilibrium is tested by giving the body a small displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to a slight displacement of the body.

rubric.why: In neutral equilibrium the body stays in its new position after displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it remains in its new position.

modelAnswer: A body is in neutral equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it remains in its new position.
Its centre of gravity stays at the same height when it is moved.

items.followUp: What is the approximate value of g on the surface of the Earth and on the Moon?

rubric.why: The approximate gravitational acceleration on the Moon is 1.6 m/s².
rubric.description: Gives the value of g on the Moon.

rubric.why: The approximate gravitational acceleration on Mars is 3.7 m/s².
rubric.description: Gives the value of g on Mars.

items.followUp: Define power and write its S.I. unit.

rubric.why: Energy is defined as the capacity to do work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that energy is the capacity or ability to do work.

rubric.why: The S.I. unit of energy is the joule.

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
Its S.I. unit is the joule (J).
